h1: The 6 Best Infrared Space Heaters of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Infrared Space Heaters 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 infrared space heaters scored on heating tech, thermostat, timers and safety features, from budget towers to Dr Infrared.
summary: The Dr Infrared DR-968 is the best infrared space heater here, combining a quartz tube with a PTC element, a remote and a 12-hour auto shut-off. The DR-998 is the step-up for bigger rooms. RealSmart's six-tube 1500W model is the value pick, while the BLACK+DECKER tower is the cheapest way to try infrared heat.
intro: Infrared heaters get sold on a claim that sounds like magic: heat that warms people instead of air. There is something to it. Radiant heat travels in a line and warms the first surface it hits, so it feels immediate at your desk or couch, but it does little for a room you are not sitting in. The mistake is buying one to heat a whole house from a corner.

So we ranked on how well each unit handles the spot-heating job, and how well it protects you while it does. We reviewed six infrared models from their listings, scoring heating technology, thermostat and timer control, remote use, coverage claims and safety features. Marketing numbers like percentage warmth gains are reported as claims, not as measured results.

products.name: Dr Infrared Heater DR-968 Portable Space Heater
products.verdict: Dual infrared quartz and PTC heating with a 12-hour auto shut-off timer and an IR remote.
products.description:
The DR-968 uses two heating systems at once: an infrared quartz tube for radiant warmth and a PTC element for convective heat. The listing adds an energy-saving mode with high and low settings, a 12-hour automatic shut-off timer and an infrared remote control.

It ranks first because the dual system covers both quick radiant warmth and gradual room heat, and the timer prevents it running all night. Against the DR-998, it costs the same $100 to $200 tier but the DR-998 claims stronger warmth. The DR-968 gets the nod for its clearer, better-documented feature set.

Buy it for a large room where you sit in one spot. The caveat: a heater this capable still cannot warm a drafty room evenly, so close doors.
products.idealFor: Large rooms where you sit near the heater for hours.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest price or whole-room heating.

products.name: DR. INFRARED HEATER DR-998
products.verdict: Claims 60 percent more warmth than standard 1500W heaters, with even heat distribution.
products.description:
The DR-998 is Dr Infrared's all-in-one comfort unit, and its listing claims 60 percent more warmth than standard 1500W heaters along with even heat distribution. That figure is a manufacturer claim, not a measurement we can confirm.

It ranks second because the listing says less about timers and control than the DR-968's detailed bullets. It sits in the same $100 to $200 tier, so the choice is about trust in documented features versus a stronger-warmth claim. For many buyers, the stated even heat distribution is the draw.

Choose it for a bigger space where you want the claimed extra warmth. The caveat: percentage claims without a test standard are marketing, so judge by owner feedback on your room size.
products.idealFor: Bigger rooms where extra warmth outweighs feature detail.
products.skipIf: You want documented timers and a remote.

products.name: RealSmart 1500W Infrared Space Heater for Indoor Use
products.verdict: Six upgraded quartz infrared tubes at 1500W for even warmth in large rooms, whisper-quiet.
products.description:
RealSmart packs six upgraded quartz infrared tubes into a 1500W heater that its listing describes as whisper-quiet, with even warmth for large rooms. Six tubes spread the radiant output across a wider panel than a single-tube design.

It ranks third because it lacks the dual heating system, remote and 12-hour timer of the DR-968. What it offers is a stated 1500W and a quiet claim at $50 to $100, half the price of the Dr Infrared models.

Buy it for a bedroom or home office where noise matters. The caveat: the listing names no thermostat, timer or tip-over detail, so confirm safety features before leaving it on unattended.
pros: Half the price of Dr Infrared
products.idealFor: Quiet bedrooms and offices that need affordable radiant heat.
products.skipIf: You want a timer and remote.

products.name: EdenPURE CopperPLUS Infrared Heaters for Indoor Use Portable 1000 Sq Ft
products.verdict: A portable infrared heater rated for 1000 sq ft with over 3.5 sq ft of copper surface and a washable filter.
products.description:
EdenPURE's CopperPLUS is positioned for up to 1000 square feet, with over 3.5 square feet of copper surface, energy cost savings claims and a lifetime washable filter. The large radiating surface is what the brand leans on.

It ranks fourth because it sits in the $200 to $500 tier, the highest here, and the coverage claim is a marketing figure. Against the DR-968, it costs more with fewer documented controls. The washable filter is a practical feature that spares you buying replacements.

Choose it if you want the largest claimed coverage and a washable filter. The caveat: a 1000 sq ft rating assumes an open, well-insulated space, and infrared heat is still directional.
products.idealFor: Open rooms where the claimed coverage and filter matter.
products.skipIf: You want timers, remotes and a lower price.

products.name: Space Heater for Indoor Use 1500W Infrared Heater
products.verdict: A 1500W infrared heater with three heat settings, a thermostat and a programmable timer.
products.description:
This 1500W infrared heater lists three heat settings, a thermostat with temperature control and a programmable timer. For $50 to $100, that is the cleanest control set outside the Dr Infrared models.

It ranks fifth because the listing is generic about heating tech and names no remote or safety certifications, and the brand is not given. Against RealSmart, it adds thermostat and timer control, but RealSmart states its six-tube design.

Buy it if you want thermostat and timer control without paying more. The caveat: with an unnamed brand and a bare listing, check owner feedback on build quality and safety before running it unattended.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want thermostat and timer control.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Infrared Radiant Quartz Tower Heater
products.verdict: A $25 to $50 infrared quartz tower with heat settings and cool-touch housing.
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's tower heater uses infrared quartz heat with multiple heat settings and a cool-touch housing, at $25 to $50. The tower shape fits narrow spots beside a chair or desk.

It ranks last because the listing names no thermostat, timer or remote, and no wattage. It is the cheapest way to test whether radiant heat suits you, and the cool-touch housing is a meaningful safety detail around children and pets.

Buy it for a small personal space on a tight budget. The caveat: with so few stated features, it is a basic heater, and you should keep clear of it with fabrics and cords.
products.idealFor: Personal spaces such as a desk or chair on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You need to warm a large room.

whatMatters.detail: Infrared heaters warm objects and people directly, while convection heaters warm the air. Radiant warmth feels instant but only where it points. Convection spreads more evenly but takes longer. Decide whether you sit in one place or want the room warm, and check the listing for the words infrared quartz or PTC.

A timer ends the heating session on its own, which matters if you fall asleep. The Dr Infrared DR-968 lists a 12-hour auto shut-off and another model lists a programmable timer. Heaters left running are a real fire risk, so treat a timer as a requirement rather than a luxury.

With a thermostat the element switches on and off around your chosen temperature, which saves electricity and avoids overheating a small room. Without one, the heater runs flat out. Look for thermostat or temperature control in the specs, as on the generic 1500W model, and note whether it is a dial or a digital setting.

Most plug-in heaters top out at 1500W, which is close to the limit of a standard household circuit. Running one alongside other appliances can trip the breaker. Check the wattage in the listing, and plug the heater straight into the wall rather than a power strip or extension cord.

Cool-touch housing, tip-over protection and overheat sensors protect children and pets. The BLACK+DECKER lists a cool-touch housing; others list less. Look for third-party safety certification in the listing, keep three feet of clear space around the unit, and never cover it.

faq.q: Do infrared heaters work in large rooms?
faq.a: They warm what they face, not the whole space. The Dr Infrared DR-968 adds a PTC element for room heat, but even then, aim it at where you sit. Close doors to hold in the warmth.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with space heaters?
faq.a: Plugging into an extension cord or power strip. A 1500W heater like the RealSmart draws close to a standard circuit's limit. Use a wall outlet directly, and keep three feet of clearance from fabrics.

faq.q: Is the Dr Infrared worth it over a cheap tower?
faq.a: If you use it daily, yes. The DR-968's 12-hour timer, remote and dual heating justify $100 to $200, while a BLACK+DECKER tower at $25 to $50 is fine for occasional desk warmth.

faq.q: How do I set up an infrared heater safely?
faq.a: Place it on a flat, hard surface facing where you sit, with clear space around it. Set the timer on models like the DR-968 before leaving it. Never leave any heater running in an empty room.
Unplug it, let it cool and dust the grille with a soft brush. On the EdenPURE CopperPLUS, wash the filter on schedule. Store heaters dry, and inspect the cord for damage each season.

faq.q: Are the percentage warmth claims reliable?
faq.a: Treat them as marketing. The DR-998's 60 percent claim and EdenPURE's 1000 sq ft rating have no test standard in the listing. Rely on wattage, controls and owner feedback from rooms like yours.

finalTake: The Dr Infrared DR-968 is the best infrared space heater for most people: dual heating, a remote and a 12-hour shut-off. The RealSmart is the better value for quiet rooms, and the BLACK+DECKER tower is the cheapest trial. Whatever you pick, plug it straight into the wall and never leave it unattended.
